title: All-Hands: Theme, Exec Updates, and Cross-Org Asks (May 2026) - Draft
content:
Purpose and high-level goal:
- Purpose: Align the company on priorities for H2 FY26, surface important cross-org asks, and land the updated OKR framing before leadership finalizes targets.
- Tone: celebratory but pragmatic — highlight wins (reliability, cost wins) while being explicit about tradeoffs and asks.

Proposed all-hands theme: "One Runtime, Many Wins"
- Messaging hook: show how our unified runtime (serving runtime + smart routing + caching) unlocked predictable performance for customers and set the stage for scale across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private.
- Visual idea: three tiles (Hosted API, Dedicated, Private) morphing into single runtime pipeline graphic; callout metrics next to each tile.

Agenda (90 min total)
- 0:00–0:05 Opening (CEO) — 1 slide: theme + big-picture momentum
- 0:05–0:15 Business update (Head of GTM) — 3 slides: revenue run rate, top customer logos, macro GTM motion (PLG -> enterprise mix)
- 0:15–0:30 Product & roadmap highlights (CTO/Product Head) — 6 slides: Redwood Console, Optimize, new model catalog features, perf snapshots
- 0:30–0:45 Engineering deep-dive (VP Eng, Serving Runtime) — 5 slides: latency P50/P95 trends, KV cache improvements, new quantization profiles, outage postmortem learnings
- 0:45–0:55 Customer success story (Customer Success) — 2 slides + 5-min customer video
- 0:55–1:05 People & org update (Head of People) — 2 slides: hiring focus, DEI milestone, new leadership hires
- 1:05–1:20 OKR framing and cross-org asks (Head of Strategy / COO) — 6 slides: proposed company OKRs, top team asks, success criteria
- 1:20–1:30 Live Q&A + closing (CEO + panel)

Key slide / content asks from teams (concrete)
- Eng (Serving Runtime): Two slides — 1) simple chart showing P50/P95 token latency trend last 6 months; 2) bullets on upcoming deploys (kernel selector rollout, continuous batching improvements), and any feature that requires org-level tradeoffs (e.g., short-term increase in mem usage for 20% latency improvement).
- Product (Hosted API / Console): One slide with three customer scenarios where Console observability prevented regressions + one bullet on dataset for demo.
- Dedicated & Private: One slide each summarizing current installs, SLA attainment, and a single ask for platform engineering (2-week windows for on-prem test clusters).
- GTM: 1 slide listing top-5 named accounts to call out + one notable customer quote.
- CS: 1 slide with customer health distribution and 2 ask items for engineering (one bugfix priority).

OKR framing (draft bullets)
- Company Objective A: Deliver predictable, production-grade inference that reduces customer per-token cost by 15% while keeping P95 latency within SLOs.
  - KR A1: Reduce average per-token cost (hosted + dedicated baselines) by 15% vs Jan 2026 baseline.
  - KR A2: Maintain P95 serving latency under target for 95% of production traffic.
  - KR A3: Ship 3 model/quantization profiles recommended by Redwood Optimize.

- Company Objective B: Expand footprint in enterprise and regulated workloads.
  - KR B1: Close 8 Dedicated or Private deals with annualized contract value >= $250k.
  - KR B2: Complete SOC2 R2 readiness checklist and 2 region deployments for Private.

- Company Objective C: Developer-first adoption and velocity.
  - KR C1: Increase API active developers (30-day) by 40% QoQ.
  - KR C2: Reduce time-to-onboard (first successful call) median from 14min to 7min.

Cross-org asks (for the audience to action)
- Product: finalize console pre-read deck by Apr 28 (asks: two short benchmarks to include).
- Engineering: freeze non-critical infra changes during the 48 hours before the all-hands rehearsal window.
- GTM: identify and confirm at least three customers willing to be on stage or on video by Apr 30.
- People Ops: finalize headcount plan snapshot for H2 by May 5.
- Legal/Security: short approval window for Private deployment demo materials (need OK within 3 business days).

Pre-reads and distribution plan
- Pre-reads to go out 7 days before: 1) Executive one-pager with OKR bullets and asks (1 page) 2) Product one-pager: key roadmap items and risks (2 pages) 3) Short metrics snapshot (1 page).
- Channel: email + #all-hands Slack thread + pinned Confluence page. Ask managers to hold skip-levels to surface questions ahead of time.

Logistics checklist (must be completed before dry run)
- AV: confirm Zoom streaming + broadcast setup, test captions, confirm recording permissions (Owner: Ops).
- Slides: consolidated deck in shared drive (single source) — MAX 25 slides total. Each presenter limited to 2–6 slides.
- Rehearsal schedule: speaker dry run on May 10 (full run), tech check May 12.
- Accessibility: provide transcript + short summary for those asynchronous.

Q&A plan and moderation
- Pre-slotted questions from Slack thread collected to start the Q&A. Panel will answer live and then open to audience via Slido for prioritization. Moderator to triage and surface the top 6 questions.

Risks and mitigation (brief)
- Risk: Too much technical detail — Mitigate: ensure product/eng speak in 60s soundbites for non-technical audience.
- Risk: Last-minute slide churn — Mitigate: slide freeze 24 hours before tech check; only emergency updates allowed.
- Risk: Customer NDA limitations — Mitigate: CS confirm shareable quotes and video rights early.

Open questions / decisions needed (please comment inline)
- Who will produce the 1-page OKR one-pager? Suggest: Strategy + People Ops.
- Finalize CEO opening note: anecdote vs metric-led — preference? (CEO to decide by Apr 25).
- Are we calling out specific Dedicated customers by name? Legal/CS to confirm shareability.

Action items (owner, due)
- Priya K: consolidate deck and circulate v0.8 by May 1.
- Liam O'C: coordinate rehearsals + AV test bookings by Apr 28.
- Jing W: assemble metrics snapshot and P95/P50 charts by Apr 26.
- Marcus R: lock down customer story consent forms by Apr 30.

Notes to self / rough brainstorm (informal)
- Consider a 30–60 sec customer video showing before/after latency/cost impacts (simple b-roll + 2 quotes).
- Might highlight a quick demo of Redwood Optimize recommending a quantization profile live — need fallback pre-recording in case of demo fail.
- Keep it human: one solid people story and one engineering win story.

Appendix (short)
- Suggested slide limits and templates: one template for exec, one for product deep-dive.
- Contact list for AV and ops: ops-support@redwood.ai, lt-ops slack channel.

Footnote: This is a working draft. Please add comments in the doc, tag owners on specific asks, and flag anything that will push the slide budget.
